correctness.rationale: For any two-sided dominating set, the least selected B-class and greatest selected A-class force every earlier A-class and later B-class into the set; these forced inclusions imply adjacent or overlapping boundary indices. The converse follows because the selected boundary classes dominate every omitted vertex. The cases with adjacent boundaries are exactly the canonical cut sets. The disjoint boundary decomposition gives the generating factors and is checked coefficient-by-coefficient on 540 canonical instances through order 11.

value.rationale: The result gives the full coefficient distribution of a classical hard-to-compute graph polynomial on a canonical structured bipartite class, not merely a minimum parameter. The unique boundary-index classification converts the nested-neighborhood structure into a direct closed enumerator, total-count formula, and domination-number corollary. The multi-class formula is structurally stronger than recomputing the known complete-bipartite case and is reusable for coefficient and root questions.
